title: Technical stitch playbook for embedded pilots (wip)
content:
PURPOSE:
Short, action-oriented playbook for sellers + SEs to run low-friction embedded pilots (proof-of-value) for customers that require tighter integration (SDK + infra handshake) and/or regulatory controls. Focus: reduce time-to-first-success, surface operational constraints early, document fallbacks and success metrics for a clean conversion to Dedicated/Private later.

INTENDED AUDIENCE:
- Sales Engineers (SE) running technical discovery and pilot setup
- Field Sellers & AE execs owning pilot outcomes
- Solutions/Platform Engineers on customer side who will do the integration

HIGH-LEVEL SELLING NARRATIVE (30s):
- Problem: customers building product features on LLMs hit inconsistent latency/cost and operational surprises during scale.
- Redwood angle: single runtime you can start embedded in a pilot, then scale to Dedicated or Private with the same APIs, plus built-in fallbacks to keep critical flows online.
- Pilot ask: 6-week technical pilot, 1 production route (small % traffic), success criteria = latency below X, cost per 1k tokens within Y, and no data egress > org policy.

QUALIFYING QUESTIONS (quick checklist):
- Target route: batch vs interactive? (chat/agent vs single-turn inference)
- P95 latency requirement? (hard stop < 300ms, soft < 600ms)
- Data residency/KMS requirements? Any need for HSM?
- Traffic shape: spikes, concurrency, sustained throughput?
- Will the customer accept a hosted sandbox or require VPC/on-prem from day 1?

PILOT DESIGN PATTERNS (pick one):
1) SDK-proxy -> Hosted sandbox (fastest)
   - Use Redwood SDK + short-lived keys, local proxy to instrument request/response, minimal infra changes.
   - Good when data sensitivity is moderate and buyer wants speed.
2) Edge-embedded inference (sidecar)
   - Lightweight sidecar that routes requests to Redwood, keeps local prefix caching, enforces local auth.
   - Good for low-latency regional needs without full VPC.
3) Private test deployment (VPC stub)
   - Early private control-plane with restricted egress, customer-managed keys. Slower but needed for regulated verticals.

TECHNICAL HANDSHAKE CHECKLIST (SE script):
- Ask for: sample request payloads (1-3 representative requests), expected token sizes, concurrency profile.
- Provide: sample SDK snippet (JS + Python) and a minimal docker sidecar example.
- Security: confirm TLS mutual auth needs, KMS provider, audit log retention window.
- Telemetry: ensure customer agrees to share synthetic traces (obfuscated) and p95 token latency for pilot review.
- Rollback plan: route-level fallback to smaller model or remote completions if latency breach.

DEMO / RUNBOOK (concise steps for SE):
1) Day 0: quick discovery call (30m) to collect qualifying answers + assign owner.
2) Day 1: share starter repo + short-lived API key + SDK snippet.
3) Day 2–7: integration window — customer runs 50–200 synthetic requests, run baseline metrics.
4) Week 2: run a 1-hour load window with real-ish data; collect latency/cost analytics.
5) Week 3–4: iterate prompt engineering and batching + enable prefix caching.
6) Week 5: final evaluation vs success criteria, decide scale or handoff to solutions.

MINIMUM SUCCESS METRICS (example targets — tune per account):
- Functional: response correctness on a 50-sample golden set (precision > 85%)
- Performance: p95 latency < 600ms interactive, average tokens/sec > X for batch
- Cost: per-1k-token cost within 20% of the customer target
- Reliability: 99.5% successful requests during a 1-hour stress test

SECURITY & COMPLIANCE FAQ (quick answers for SE):
- Q: Do we see raw customer data? A: For hosted pilots we only persist telemetry and obfuscated traces unless a retention agreement is in place. Private deployments can use customer-managed KMS and keep data on their network.
- Q: Can we sign an NDA + DPA? A: Yes, legal owns standard DPA; for regulated verticals escalate to security-compliance early.
- Q: Audit logs? A: Enable full audit logging in Private, limited trace logs for Hosted sandbox.

COMMON OBJECTIONS & SCRIPTS:
- "We need absolute latency guarantees." -> "We can start with sidecar + caching pattern to absorb first-mile latency; commit to a canary SLA for pilot so we measure and tune kernel selection/batching."
- "We can’t send data to hosted services." -> "Offer VPC stub pilot or provide a small on-prem preview package; meanwhile use token anonymization and contract terms to reduce risk."

EMAIL TEMPLATES (copy/paste):
- Subject: Quick pilot proposal — 6-week embed test to validate latency + cost
- Body: Hi {Name}, following our call, attaching a 6-week technical pilot plan: we provide an SDK snippet, short-lived keys, and a small sidecar you can drop in. Goal: validate p95 latency and cost per 1k tokens on representative traffic. Suggest kickoff on {date}. -- Anita

KNOWN RISKS & MITIGATIONS (notes to SE):
- Long token sizes blow cost — recommend artificial truncation + hybrid retrieval for large context.
- Unexpected concurrency surges — use circuit-breaker and configure burst autoscale thresholds.
- Security governance delays — escalate to security-compliance with exact KMS questions (sample template in linked_artifacts).

NEXT STEPS & OWNERSHIP (template):
- AE: secure pilot scope + timeline (owner: AE name)
- SE: run discovery, share starter repo, own Day 1–7 integration (owner: SE name)
- Solutions Eng: if Private required, open security intake within 48 hours (owner: Solutions Eng)

OPEN ITEMS / TODOs:
- TODO: create a 1-click sandbox provisioning script for SEs (owner: eng-devexp)
- TODO: finalize canned audit log sample for Hosted pilots (owner: security)
- Question: what is final handoff bundle for ready-to-scale customers? define checklist.

APPENDIX (links + quick snippets):
- Starter JS snippet: https://github.com/redwood-inference/pilot-integration-samples (see /js-proxy)
- Confluence play: https://redwood.atlassian.net/wiki/spaces/GT/pages/98765
- Jira: PILOT-274 (pilot orchestration template)

NOTES / WORKING THOUGHTS:
- Keep this doc intentionally tactical and short. We will iterate with real pilot feedback; mark anything that caused friction in the pilot as a "pilot hazard" and add to internal tracker.
- Consider a compact "pilot safety checklist" card for AE wallet to carry into procurement conversations.

END
